newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN SEES GOVERNMENT WINNING CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN SEES GOVERNMENT WINNING CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday he expected his five-party left-right-green government to win a confidence vote in parliament later in the day.
"The fact that the parliamentary group have reached agreement ... gives reason to expect that the proposal ... will be approved," Lipponen told a Reuters reporter.

He was asked about the third reading vote due today at 1300/1100 GMT in parliament on a government proposal to liberalise retail store opening hours. Lipponen himself in December turned the issue into a vote of confidence.
The confidence vote will be the fifth in Lipponen's left-right-green coalition since it took office in April 1995.
Already a week ago, officials of the parliamentary groups of the three biggest government parties said it was clear that the coalition would win the confidence vote.
Leaders of the five government parties' parliamentary groups had earlier reached a compromise on the controversial draft bill to extend retail stores' possibilities to keep open on Sundays.
The bill now up for approval or rejection would allow shops to be open on Sundays in June, July, August and December and on five other Sundays to be defined later.
Lipponen turned the issue into a vote of confidence after the proposal had suffered a surprise defeat in parliament. The bill was narrowly rejected, by 84 votes to 82.
Of the five government parties' 142 MPs, 36 voted against the proposal. Of those, 20 were from Lipponen's own Social Democratic Party.
